body: Emirates announced on November 9, 2026 that it is opening its Centre of Hospitality Excellence in Dubai to companies in the United Arab Emirates. UAE organizations can now book courses of one to five days at the center, and according to Emirates, government entities, universities and regional companies have already taken part since it began running external programs. The US$8 million facility was unveiled in October 2025 as a training facility for the airline's roughly 25,000 cabin crew, with more than 10,000 expected to train there by the end of that year.

The center sits within the Emirates Crew Training Centre and includes a restaurant and lounge for up to 170 guests, presentation kitchens, eight classrooms and a training kitchen modeled partly on an aircraft galley. It grew out of a 2020 partnership with Switzerland's Ecole hôtelière de Lausanne, which helped Emirates define its service approach around four values: excellence, attentiveness, innovation and passion. It opened seven months after the airline launched a 24/7 Crew Zone at its Dubai headquarters in March 2025. Organizations can choose from modules on hospitality fundamentals, fine dining service and etiquette, wine taught by WSET Level 3-certified trainers, culinary techniques with Emirates chefs, team-building, and leadership sessions with Emirates executives. Tours of the airline's training facilities, including its aircraft simulators, are also offered, and programs can be customized; Emirates did not disclose pricing.

Cabin crew remain the center's core trainees. Thomas Ney, Divisional Senior Vice President Service Delivery at Emirates, said the airline wanted to share expertise built up over decades: "Delivering exceptional hospitality requires more than technical training." All cabin crew complete an eight-week program at the Crew Training Centre covering safety, security, medical care and service; at the hospitality center, crew are also served a four-course meal of First and Business Class dishes as guests, practice plating, and take part in a three-level wine program introduced in 2024.
en.summary: Emirates is opening its Centre of Hospitality Excellence in Dubai — an $8 million facility built for its roughly 25,000 cabin crew — to UAE businesses, offering one- to five-day courses in hospitality, fine dining, wine and leadership.
en.title: Emirates opens $8 million Dubai cabin crew hospitality hub to UAE businesses

body: 阿聯酋航空11月9日宣布，將杜拜的卓越款待中心（Centre of Hospitality Excellence）對阿拉伯聯合大公國企業開放，阿聯機構可預訂1至5天的課程；據阿聯酋航空表示，政府機關、大學與地區企業在對外課程開辦後已經參與。該中心耗資800萬美元，2025年10月揭幕，原為約2萬5000名客艙組員而建，當時預計2025年底前有逾1萬人受訓。

中心位於阿聯酋航空機組員訓練中心內，設有可容納170名賓客的餐廳與貴賓室、示範廚房、8間教室，以及部分仿照飛機廚房設計的訓練廚房。中心源自2020年與瑞士洛桑酒店管理學院（Ecole hôtelière de Lausanne）的合作，以卓越、細心、創新與熱情四項價值定義服務理念；中心在阿聯酋航空2025年3月於杜拜總部啟用全天候機組員專區（Crew Zone）七個月後開幕。課程包括款待基礎、精緻餐飲服務與禮儀、葡萄酒（由WSET第3級認證講師授課）、與阿聯酋航空主廚學習烹飪技巧、團隊建立，以及與高階主管的領導課程；亦提供訓練設施導覽（包括模擬機），課程可客製化，價格未公開。

客艙組員仍是中心的核心學員。阿聯酋航空服務交付部門資深副總裁Thomas Ney表示，希望分享數十年累積的專業：「Delivering exceptional hospitality requires more than technical training」。所有客艙組員都在機組員訓練中心完成8週課程，涵蓋安全、保安、醫療與服務；在款待中心，組員還會以賓客身分享用頭等與商務艙菜色組成的4道菜餐點、練習擺盤，並參加2024年推出的3級葡萄酒課程。
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空宣布，將杜拜的卓越款待中心對阿聯企業開放，可預訂1至5天的課程；該中心耗資800萬美元，於2025年10月揭幕，原為約2萬5000名客艙組員而設。
zh.title: 阿聯酋航空800萬美元客艙服務培訓中心對阿聯企業開放
